text:
jonathan: Heads-up — starting ~09:10 UTC we saw a cluster spike in GPU resets, mostly Xid 13 and Xid 31 across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Noticing degraded p50 latency for short-chat workloads.
sara: saw it too, dashboards show a correlated increase in decode errors and a burst of small batch traffic from tenant set 'nlp-lite'.
min: possible noisy-neighbor. Which models were hot? any version pins?
jonathan: model-gen v2 pinned on dedicated pools in both regions, traffic pattern: many short 1-3 token queries at high QPS.
ops-bot: deploy finished: rollout/2026-03-18/model-gen-v2 to eu-west-1 at 09:02 UTC.
kevin: can someone paste the dmesg lines? want to check if it's NVRM Xid 13 followed by GPU reset or ECC?
irina: paste from rack-3b GPU node-17: ```Mar 18 09:11:06 kernel: NVRM: Xid (13) at 0x3c4f0b: PID 4212: GPU exception on engine 0.```
jonathan: also saw this sequence: ```Mar 18 09:11:06 kernel: GPU 0: Load: decode thread crash -> reset
Mar 18 09:11:06 kernel: pcieport 0000:03:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: ID 00a0```
sara: interesting — AER corrected errors on PCIe alongside Xid. could be NIC/PCIe transient causing GPU reset cascades.
min: check NIC flaps around the same time. I pulled ifup logs from the host: ```09:10:58 NIC eth0: link down
09:11:04 NIC eth0: link up```
kevin: that timing matches. NIC flap -> PCIe AER -> NVRM Xid 13/31 sequence is plausible.
irina: hardware telemetry for node-17 shows no persistent ECC counts increase (ECC correctable stays low). so not classic ECC degradation.
jonathan: action plan suggestion: 1) drain affected GPUs (rack-3b node-17/18) 2) run memtest + stress for PCIe + re-seat NIC 3) if repeat, schedule card replacement.
sara: agree. also add routing policy to shift short-chat tenant traffic away from dedicated pools during investigation (canary to hosted).
min: cost check — moving 200 qps of short chats to hosted for 6 hours estimate: ~ $1200 (bandwidth + tokens). ok?
kevin: fine for incident hours, prioritize availability > cost.
jonathan: I'm running live drain on node-17 now: `fleetctl drain node-17 --reason "xid13-pcie-flap"`
ops-bot: node-17: drain started by jonathan at 09:18 UTC. current running: 3 jobs, eviction in progress.
irina: started a stress run on node-18 memory/pcie lanes: `stress-ng --matrix 0 --iomix 1h` and `pcie-memtest --device 0000:03:00.0 --run 1000`
sara: quick triage note: checks to run before replacing card — a) reproduce NIC flap (swap cable) b) update kernel/NVRM drivers if older than 530.xx c) test same workload with batching disabled (we saw more resets with tiny batches)
min: I patched autoscaler to avoid micro-bursting short chats into dedicated pools for next 24h.
kevin: logging: can we add a quick alert for AER events on GPU hosts? those are useful precursors.
jonathan: agreed, opened alert rule: `gpu.aer.events > 0` with 5m window, severity P2.
sara: thanks. I'll follow-up after stress runs finish (~10:10 UTC). if node-18 is clean, we'll bring node-17 back and monitor for 2h before hardware ops.
kevin: for postmortem: include tenant list, burst QPS histograms, driver versions, and PCIe AER counts.
jonathan: noted. tagging hardware-ops for replacement hold if we re-hit Xid 13 within 48h. @hardware-ops FYI.
ops-bot: incident: 2026-03-18-09:10-gpu-reset-spike created and linked to this thread.
min: moving short-chat traffic now, will post cost charge later.
sara: update 09:55 UTC — node-18 stress passed, no repeat. node-17 drained and re-provisioned, brought up with fresh cable and updated driver 535.54.03. monitoring.
jonathan: final: by 11:30 UTC resets back to baseline, no further Xid patterns. leaving alert on for 24h. closing incident in 48h if stable. :thumbsup:
